page: UpCloud PREMIUM-2xCPU-8GB is a general-purpose virtual server configured with 2 shared vCPUs and 8 GB of system memory, maintaining a standard 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio. The instance is powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor running on the x86_64 architecture at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The virtual environment operates under the KVM hypervisor and incorporates 16 MB of L3 cache, along with support for vector extensions including AVX-512 (VNNI and BF16) and cryptographic hardware acceleration via AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

Storage and networking provisions include 100 GB of bundled local SSD storage and a single complimentary public IPv4 address. The server does not include dedicated graphics processing units. In performance evaluations, the AMD EPYC 9575F delivers exceptional single-core compute results, achieving top-tier ratings in stress-ng single-core tests, Geekbench single-core execution (2278.0), single-threaded gzip compression, and text processing. However, multi-core throughput scales modestly across its two shared cores, with Geekbench multi-core results and multi-threaded decompression falling into lower percentiles.

Memory bandwidth measurements demonstrate standard cached read rates, but large-block write operations and synthetic memory benchmarks register lower efficiency. Similarly, operational throughput in memory-bound services such as Redis shows constrained execution capacity. This architecture offers balanced utility for tasks requiring robust per-thread execution speed without demanding high multi-threaded parallelism, making it cost-efficient for lightweight web serving, application staging, microservices, and modest enterprise automation routines.
description: UpCloud PREMIUM-2xCPU-8GB is a balanced general-purpose virtual machine equipped with 2 shared vCPUs on an AMD EPYC 9575F processor, 8 GB of RAM, and 100 GB of local SSD storage. Built on the x86_64 architecture with KVM virtualization, it features hardware support for AVX-512 instruction sets and cryptographic acceleration. Benchmark results demonstrate standout single-thread compute capabilities, scoring in the top tier for single-core stress-ng tests, Geekbench single-core evaluations, and single-threaded data compression. In contrast, multi-core throughput and uncached memory write bandwidth remain modest due to the two-core shared configuration. The server includes one complimentary public IPv4 address and operates without dedicated GPU hardware. With its standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory profile and strong per-core responsiveness, it is best suited for lightweight web serving, microservices, staging environments, and basic utility applications.
